rounds.text: Infollion Research Services Ltd trades at a compelling P/E ratio of just 12.3x [E1], representing a stark discount to the sector benchmark P/E of 19.94x [E6]. This valuation disconnect is further highlighted by an exceptional return on equity of 18.67%, which dwarfs the sector benchmark of 4.82% [E8]. Fundamental valuation work reinforces this mispricing, as a discounted cash flow model puts intrinsic value at Rs 547 per share compared to the current market price of ₹ 159 [E39], translating to a massive margin of safety of 70.9% [E40]. Moreover, a reverse DCF reveals that the current market price implies an annualized earnings growth of a mere 0.9%, sitting drastically below the base case assumption of 18.0% [E41].

While the headline P/E ratio sits at a seemingly modest 12.3x [E1], the market price of ₹ 159 leaves the stock sitting just 1% of the way up its 52-week range of ₹ 155 to ₹ 551 [E5], signalling severe and ongoing downward momentum rather than a stable bargain. Furthermore, Infollion's price-to-book ratio of 2.32x demands a premium over the sector benchmark of 1.51x [E7], meaning investors are paying an inflated multiple on net assets despite the steep collapse in share price. Income-seeking investors receive zero support from the stock, as the dividend yield stands flat at 0.00% [E4]. Conceded: the business generates a strong ROE of 18.67% compared to the sector benchmark of 4.82% [E8], and a discounted cash flow model suggests a large margin of safety [E39, E40, E41]. However, this historical return does not insulate shareholders from the risk of a value trap when price erosion is this extreme and distributions are entirely absent [E4, E5].

Conceded: the dividend yield stands at 0.00% [E4] and the stock sits at 1% of its 52-week range [E5]. However, that severe price drop to ₹ 159 [E2, E39] places the equity at a modest P/E ratio of 12.3x [E1], which is discounted relative to the sector benchmark P/E of 19.94x [E6]. This compressed valuation contrasts sharply with an exceptional ROE of 18.67% that vastly outperforms the sector benchmark of 4.82% [E8]. Far from being an inflated multiple, the price-to-book ratio of 2.30x [E2] is fully justified by this superior capital efficiency. Most decisively, a discounted cash flow model establishes an intrinsic value yielding a substantial margin of safety of 70.9% [E39, E40], while a reverse DCF proves the market price only prices in a negligible 0.9% earnings growth rate [E41].

Conceded: the P/E ratio is 12.3x [E1] and ROE is 18.67% [E8]. However, the bull's heavy reliance on the scanX DCF intrinsic value of ₹ 547 [E39] and the resulting 70.9% margin of safety [E40] ignores the alarming reality that the stock sits at just 1% of its 52-week high, having plummeted from a peak of ₹ 551 to ₹ 159 [E5]. While the reverse DCF suggests the market only prices in 0.9% earnings growth [E41], this extreme downward momentum and proximity to the 551 high's floor (at the ₹ 155 low) [E5] signals severe underlying distress or a complete loss of market confidence that a simple model cannot wish away. Furthermore, the bull defends the 2.30x P/B ratio [E2] using high ROE [E8], but ignores that this P/B multiple trades at a significant premium to the sector benchmark of 1.51x [E7]. Finally, the complete absence of any dividend yield at 0.00% [E4] means shareholders are absorbing all of this downward price volatility with zero cash return.
